> AI-driven multi-format SVG content generation system. Converts source documents into high-quality SVG pages through multi-role collaboration and exports to PPTX.

**Core Pipeline**: `Source Document → Create Project → Template Option → Strategist → [Image_Generator] → Executor → Post-processing → Export`

> [!CAUTION]
> ## 🚨 Global Execution Discipline (MANDATORY)
>
> **This workflow is a strict serial pipeline. The following rules have the highest priority — violating any one of them constitutes execution failure:**
>
> 1. **SERIAL EXECUTION** — Steps MUST be executed in order; the output of each step is the input for the next. Non-BLOCKING adjacent steps may proceed continuously once prerequisites are met, without waiting for the user to say "continue"
> 2. **BLOCKING = CONFIRMATION POINT** — Steps marked ⛔ BLOCKING are confirmation checkpoints. If a user is present, pause and wait for confirmation. If no user is available (e.g. automated / non-interactive mode), the AI should make professional recommendations based on the source material and proceed automatically

> 5. **NO SPECULATIVE EXECUTION** — "Pre-preparing" content for subsequent Steps is FORBIDDEN (e.g., writing SVG code during the Strategist phase)
> 6. **NO SUB-AGENT SVG GENERATION** — Executor Step 6 SVG generation is context-dependent and MUST be completed by the current main agent end-to-end. Delegating page SVG generation to sub-agents is FORBIDDEN

# Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Software Tasks: Time Horizon Doubling Every 7 Months

## Source
- URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.14499
- Authors: Thomas Kwa, Ben West, Joel Becker, et al. — Model Evaluation & Threat Research (METR)
- Published: March 2025

## The Time Horizon Metric

The paper proposes a new metric for quantifying AI autonomous capabilities: the **50% task-completion time horizon** — the duration of tasks (measured by how long they take skilled human professionals) that an AI model can complete with 50% success rate. This provides an intuitive, human-grounded measure of real-world AI capability that allows comparison across vastly different models (e.g., GPT-2 vs. Claude 3.7 Sonnet).

The methodology involves three steps: (1) assembling a diverse suite of 170 software/research tasks, (2) timing skilled humans and measuring AI agent success rates on these tasks, and (3) fitting a logistic model to estimate the task duration at which each AI agent achieves 50% success.

![Methodology overview](./assets/figure_2.jpg)

## Task Suite: 170 Tasks from 1 Second to 8 Hours

The benchmark combines three task suites: HCAST (97 diverse software tasks, 1 min–30 hrs), RE-Bench (7 difficult ML research engineering tasks, all 8 hrs), and Software Atomic Actions / SWAA (66 short single-step tasks, 1 sec–30 sec). Over 800 human baselines totaling 2,529 hours were collected.

| Family | Human Time | Description |
|---|---|---|
| find_shell_script | 3 seconds | Multiple choice: "Which file is a shell script?" |
| wikipedia_research | 1 minute | Research simple factual information from Wikipedia |
| oxdna_simple | 9 minutes | Detect and fix a bug in molecular dynamics simulation input files |
| munge_data | 56 minutes | Write a Python script to transform JSON data by inferring conversion rules |
| cuda_backtesting | 8 hours | Implement custom CUDA kernels for 30x speedup of a backtesting tool |

cat > /app/benchmark/source_brief.md_ppt169_20260420/notes/total.md << 'EOF'
# Slide 1
This briefing summarizes METR's March 2025 analysis of autonomous AI software-task capability. The headline result is that the 50% task-completion time horizon has doubled roughly every 207 days, or about seven months. In concrete terms, capability moved from GPT-2 at around two seconds in 2019 to o3 at approximately one hour fifty minutes in 2025.

# Slide 2
The time-horizon metric asks a practical question: how long a task, measured in skilled-human completion time, can a model finish with 50 percent success. The methodology has three steps: assemble diverse tasks, collect human timing and model outcomes, and fit a logistic curve to estimate the 50 percent crossing point. This provides an interpretable capability scale across very different model generations.

# Slide 3
The benchmark includes 170 tasks from three sources. HCAST contributes 97 diverse software tasks with durations from one minute to thirty hours. RE-Bench adds seven difficult ML engineering tasks at eight hours. SWAA contributes 66 atomic actions from one to thirty seconds. Example tasks span from find_shell_script at three seconds up to cuda_backtesting at eight hours, grounded by over 800 human baselines and 2,529 hours of measurements.

# Slide 4
The central empirical result is an exponential trend from 2019 to 2025 with R-squared 0.97. The 50 percent horizon rises from about two seconds for GPT-2, to about five minutes for GPT-4 (0314), to approximately one hour fifty minutes for o3. The implied doubling time is about 207 days. This creates a compact, quantitative view of capability progress across release eras.

# Slide 5
Per-model success curves show that success probability decreases as task duration grows for every model. Frontier systems shift the curve rightward, meaning they retain useful success at longer durations. Claude 3.7 Sonnet and o3 substantially extend the time range relative to older systems such as GPT-2. The paper also reports that the 80 percent horizon follows a similar pattern, though at roughly one-fifth the 50 percent horizon length.

# Slide 6
The paper attributes progress to four capability clusters: stronger reasoning, more effective tool use, higher reliability and self-awareness, and better error adaptation. These traits support longer-horizon execution on multi-step technical tasks. A major limitation remains performance on less structured, messier tasks, where success is materially lower and harder to generalize.

# Slide 7
A naive extrapolation of the fitted trend suggests the one-month horizon threshold, around 167 work hours, could be reached between mid-2028 and mid-2031. The source also notes that growth from 2023 to 2025 appears about 20 percent faster than the aggregate 2019 to 2025 rate. However, this projection is uncertain because external validity and future trend stability are unresolved.

# Slide 8
Five implications follow. First, the 50 percent horizon is a strong tracking metric with high fit quality. Second, progress is fast, with approximately seven-month doubling and signs of acceleration. Third, frontier capability now approaches two-hour autonomous tasks. Fourth, external validity to real labor remains open. Fifth, limitations on unstructured tasks persist. Governance should therefore move toward tighter evaluation cadence, explicit capability thresholds, and deployment controls before longer-horizon autonomy arrives.
EOF
